stories.headline: United States and Canada close to tariff relief deal, American trade representative says
stories.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that Washington and Ottawa are making substantial progress and are relatively close to reaching an agreement on trade and tariff relief. The discussions take place amid heightened cross-border economic tensions and American scrutiny regarding Chinese influence and investments. Securing an arrangement remains a primary objective for Canadian officials seeking to protect cross-border commerce and manufacturing stability.

stories.headline: Federal government faces criticism as projections show Canada will miss 2030 climate targets
stories.summary: Official projections indicate that Canada is increasingly unlikely to meet its 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction target established under the Paris climate agreement. Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin faces growing criticism for insisting commitments remain on track, despite previous federal acknowledgments that domestic emissions will rise in the near term. Environmental organizations and opposition critics are calling on Ottawa to account for recent policy rollbacks and present realistic climate plans.

stories.headline: Daily cannabis use now surpasses daily alcohol drinking among younger Canadians, study shows
stories.summary: A study published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal has found that daily cannabis consumption now exceeds daily alcohol drinking among Canadian adults under age 50. Researchers identified a notable generational shift in consumption habits, observing that daily cannabis use among adults under 35 also surpasses daily cigarette smoking. Public health experts warn that high-frequency use carries significant medical risks, including increased susceptibility to dependency and cannabis-induced psychosis.

stories.headline: Tech companies and law enforcement clash in Senate over federal data access bill
stories.summary: Major technology corporations and law enforcement agencies have delivered opposing final appeals as the Senate debates contentious national security legislation. The proposed law would alter how digital platforms retain and disclose customer data to Canadian police and national security agencies. Law enforcement officials argue the powers are urgently needed to conduct modern criminal investigations, while tech firms warn the framework undermines basic digital privacy protections.

articles.author: Catharine Tunney
articles.title: Big tech, law enforcement make final pitches as Senate considers data access bill's future

stories.headline: Federal government begins recruiting commissioners for independent wrongful-conviction review body
stories.summary: The federal government has initiated the recruitment process for commissioners to lead the newly created Miscarriage of Justice Review Commission. The independent civilian body will be tasked with reviewing claims of wrongful conviction and deciding whether cases warrant referral back to the justice system for new trials or appeals. The commission was designed to replace the former ministerial review system and remove political decision-making from potential miscarriages of justice.

articles.author: The Canadian Press
articles.title: Ottawa recruiting commissioners for wrongful-conviction review body

stories.headline: Federal budget restrictions to Canadian cadet program prompt nationwide pushback from families
stories.summary: Parents, cadets, and community leaders across several provinces are protesting federal spending limits that have forced the suspension of several activities in the Canadian cadet program. The Department of National Defence has maintained that foundational weekly training sessions will continue unaffected despite the operational reductions. Online petitions and local appeals are urging Ottawa to reverse the funding cuts, citing the program's vital role in youth development and leadership training.

stories.headline: Bombardier aerospace workers vote overwhelmingly in favour of strike mandate
stories.summary: Workers at aircraft manufacturer Bombardier have voted by 97.8 per cent in favour of a strike mandate after rejecting the company's latest contract proposal. The unionized employees are seeking improvements in compensation and working conditions across the company's manufacturing operations. The strong strike mandate increases pressure on management to return to the bargaining table and avoid disruptions to aircraft production.

stories.headline: Navdeep Bains takes helm of Ontario Liberals at Queen's Park without legislative seat
stories.summary: Newly chosen Ontario Liberal Leader Navdeep Bains appeared with his caucus at Queen’s Park following a narrow leadership contest victory over MPP Lee Fairclough. Bains does not currently hold a seat in the provincial legislature, though he has pledged to run in an upcoming byelection or general election. At the same time, Premier Doug Ford's Progressive Conservatives are preparing targeted advertising campaigns against the former federal minister as he attempts to rebuild the party.

stories.headline: Ontario task force calls for centralized navigation system to support dementia patients
stories.summary: A healthcare task force has published a blueprint urging the Ontario government to create a centralized care navigation system for people diagnosed with dementia. Families across the province report significant barriers in accessing existing support services, often receiving little guidance on available community resources after an initial diagnosis. The proposed registry and coordination model aims to connect patients and caregivers with programs earlier to reduce caregiver burnout and acute hospital visits.

articles.author: Moira Welsh
articles.title: A dementia diagnosis — and then nothing: Ontario families struggle to find care

stories.headline: Ontario to provide Toronto $29 million for crossing guards following speed camera ban
stories.summary: The Ontario government is set to provide the City of Toronto with a one-time grant of nearly $30 million to help fund municipal crossing guards. The top-up is designed to replace revenue that was previously collected through automated speed enforcement cameras, which the Ford government banned across the province in November 2025. Municipal officials and safety advocates had expressed serious alarm that the elimination of speed cameras created significant budget deficits and jeopardized pedestrian safety around schools.

articles.author: Isaac Callan
articles.title: Toronto to receive $29M top-up for crossing guards speed cameras used to fund

stories.headline: Students and faculty organize to protect York University's Glendon campus from closure
stories.summary: Students and faculty members at York University are mobilizing against an administrative proposal to shut down the historic Glendon campus as a standalone faculty. University administrators initiated the structural review following sustained declines in enrolment at the bilingual midtown Toronto institution. Advocates argue that ending Glendon's independent status would critically erode bilingual post-secondary education and cultural offerings in southern Ontario.

articles.author: Janet Hurley
articles.title: The fate of York U’s Glendon campus will soon be decided. Students and teachers are fighting to keep it

stories.headline: Internal harassment dispute and leaked recordings create turmoil within Toronto's CUPE Local 79
stories.summary: Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 79, which represents more than 20,000 municipal workers in Toronto, is dealing with severe internal controversy involving harassment claims, covert recordings, and anonymous social media campaigns. The feud has exposed deep fractures within the executive leadership of the city's largest municipal labour organization. The leadership crisis comes as the union faces key public service obligations and internal calls for institutional reform.

articles.author: Ben Spurr
articles.title: Inside the toxic feud roiling Toronto’s largest city union: secret recordings, cheating allegations — and Lisa ‘Left Eye’ Lopes
